capture.final_message:
Use invariance of colimits under equivalence of diagrams and indexing categories.

- A natural isomorphism \(K₁ \cong K₂\) induces an equivalence between their cocone categories, preserving and reflecting colimit cocones. Applying \(F\) respects the induced isomorphism, so \(F\) preserves the colimit of \(K₁\) exactly when it preserves the colimit of \(K₂\). This gives the first conjunct without requiring either colimit to exist in advance.

- For \(e : J \simeq J'\) and any \(K : J' \to C\), restrict \(K\) along \(e.functor : J \to J'\). Equivalence of indexing categories gives
  \[
  \operatorname{PreservesColimit}(K,F)
  \;\Longleftrightarrow\;
  \operatorname{PreservesColimit}(e.functor \mathbin{\circ} K,F).
  \]
  The assumed `PreservesColimitsOfShape J F` handles the restricted diagram; transport across this equivalence yields preservation for \(K\). Quantifying over all \(K : J' \to C\) constructs `PreservesColimitsOfShape J' F`.

The useful intermediate goals are therefore iso-invariance of `PreservesColimit` and reindexing-invariance along an equivalence. The quasi-inverse and unit/counit of \(e\) supply all required diagram isomorphisms.
